# nsresolver_record (Resource)

One DNS record in an NSResolver zone. A name can hold several records of one type (e.g. two `A` records for round robin): use one resource per record.

Values are compared in NSResolver's stored form, so e.g. `mail.example.net.` and `mail.example.net` are the same answer.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "nsresolver_record" "apex" {
  zone   = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type   = "A"
  name   = "@"
  answer = "203.0.113.10"
  ttl    = 300
}

# Two A records for one name: one resource each.
resource "nsresolver_record" "mail_1" {
  zone   = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type   = "A"
  name   = "mail"
  answer = "203.0.113.20"
}

resource "nsresolver_record" "mail_2" {
  zone   = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type   = "A"
  name   = "mail"
  answer = "203.0.113.21"
}

resource "nsresolver_record" "www" {
  zone   = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type   = "CNAME"
  name   = "www"
  answer = "example.com"
}

resource "nsresolver_record" "mx" {
  zone     = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type     = "MX"
  name     = "@"
  answer   = "mail.example.com"
  priority = 10
}

resource "nsresolver_record" "spf" {
  zone   = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type   = "TXT"
  name   = "@"
  answer = "v=spf1 mx -all"
}

resource "nsresolver_record" "sip" {
  zone     = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type     = "SRV"
  name     = "_sip._tcp"
  answer   = "sip.example.com"
  priority = 10
  weight   = 5
  port     = 5060
}

resource "nsresolver_record" "caa" {
  zone   = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type   = "CAA"
  name   = "@"
  tag    = "issue"
  answer = "letsencrypt.org"
}

# Delegate a subdomain to other nameservers.
resource "nsresolver_record" "dev_ns" {
  zone   = nsresolver_zone.example.name
  type   = "NS"
  name   = "dev"
  answer = "ns1.other-provider.net"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `answer` (String) The record's value: an IPv4 address (A), IPv6 address (AAAA), hostname (CNAME, MX, SRV, NS; `.` for a null MX or SRV), text (TXT, unquoted) or CAA value (e.g. `letsencrypt.org`).
- `name` (String) Name relative to the zone, e.g. `www` or `_sip._tcp`; `@` for the zone itself.
- `type` (String) Record type: `A`, `AAAA`, `CNAME`, `MX`, `TXT`, `SRV`, `CAA`, `NS`. Changing it replaces the record.
- `zone` (String) The zone the record belongs to, e.g. `nsresolver_zone.example.name`. Changing it replaces the record.

### Optional

- `flags` (Number) CAA: flags, `0` or `128` (critical). Defaults to 0 for CAA records.
- `port` (Number) SRV: port, 0–65535. Required for SRV.
- `priority` (Number) MX and SRV: priority, 0–65535. Required for those types.
- `tag` (String) CAA: `issue`, `issuewild`, `iodef` or `issuemail`. Required for CAA.
- `ttl` (Number) TTL in seconds, 60–604800. Left out: the zone's default TTL when the record is created.
- `weight` (Number) SRV: weight, 0–65535. Required for SRV.

### Read-Only

- `fqdn` (String) The record's full name, e.g. `www.example.com`.
- `id` (String) The record's id in NSResolver.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A record is imported by "<zone>/<record id>". Find ids with the nsresolver_records data
# source, or the API: curl https://api.nsresolver.com/v1/example.com/ -H "NSToken: $NSRESOLVER_TOKEN"
terraform import nsresolver_record.www example.com/1234
```
